subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw make `mode="session"` a non-thread persistent session contract, or keep `mode="session"` reserved for thread-bound sessions and add a separate persistence/affinity path?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the permanent API controls session ownership, message routing, output visibility, cleanup, and ACP security boundaries; automation should not choose those semantics.

options.title: Design unified headless sessions
options.body: Make non-thread persistence a first-class native and ACP contract with explicit parent-relay, session targeting, lifecycle, and safety rules before implementation.

options.title: Keep session mode thread-bound
options.body: Preserve the current docs/tests/runtime contract and direct users toward `mode="run"`, `sessions_send`, or channel thread support instead.

options.title: Split ACP affinity first
options.body: Implement the narrower ACP affinity design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55484 before deciding whether native subagents share the same contract.

recommendation.title: Design unified headless sessions
recommendation.body: Make non-thread persistence a first-class native and ACP contract with explicit parent-relay, session targeting, lifecycle, and safety rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent core thread-binding refactor makes this the best available routing owner for the product/API direction.
